lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Quiet can be revealing in August - and in Toronto, the silence is doing a lot of talking. The biggest fresh note is the Leafs naming Patrick O'Sullivan director of NHL development, a small hire on paper but a clear signal about how seriously they're treating the pipeline. The club also keeps surfacing in Patrik Laine chatter, which tells you the front office is still hunting for scoring help even in a market that rarely hands out bargains. After finishing 32-36-14, this is no time for nostalgia or spin; it's time to patch holes and sharpen the next wave. Max Domi's recovery remains a watch item, and that matters because depth up front can vanish fast. What to watch next: whether Toronto turns rumor into a real addition before camp opens.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays' summer has turned into a roster jigsaw, and the latest piece clicked in only after a long rule check in New York produced a run for Boston - a reminder that chaos still finds this club. Toronto answered by shuffling the deck again, selecting Simeon Woods Richardson and recalling Charles McAdoo while sending Lazaro Estrada and Davis Schneider back to Buffalo, with Willie MacIver designated for assignment. The club sits in the offseason now, its final record frozen at 88-74, and the noise is all about construction, not games. Jameson Taillon's forearm discomfort only sharpened the urgency around a rotation already missing Trey Yesavage and Spencer Arrighetti. What matters next is whether Toronto can stabilize the pitching staff before camp and decide which of these revolving-door roster bets actually sticks.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Quiet can be deceiving, and Toronto's offseason has turned into a waiting room with a very loud name on the door. The Kawhi Leonard-to-Raptors deal remains on hold as the league's investigation drags on - the kind of uncertainty that can freeze a front office and reshape the whole plan. For now, the Raptors sit in the deep offseason with no games to chase, only decisions to make: if Leonard lands, the rotation changes overnight; if he doesn't, the depth chart looks very different. Jamal Shead is one of the cleaner storylines left - can he find a go-to scoring move and carve out a real role? That matters in a season that is already being built from the margins. What happens with Leonard before camp will tell you everything about Toronto's next move.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: Camp has turned on a dime in Ashburn. One day the Commanders were sorting out the usual summer clutter; the next, Laremy Tunsil's torn triceps and surgery ripped the left side of the line wide open and shoved Brandon Coleman back to left tackle, where he now has to hold the fort. That is the headline, and it has changed everything - from Jayden Daniels' protection to how they project the whole front. The first unofficial depth chart only sharpened the intrigue, with Luke McCaffrey getting a quiet vote of confidence and the kicking race still sputtering. Washington is in training camp, not the regular season, and that distinction matters: this is about building a 53, not chasing ghosts. Watch Coleman at left tackle, McCaffrey's role in the slot, and how quickly the new line settles before preseason snaps start.

article.title: Tuesday's Skate
paragraphs: The Leafs are deep in offseason opinion season, with one preview calling for big years from Auston Matthews and William Nylander and another putting prospect Patriks Plumins at No. 16 in the system. The most concrete Leafs wrinkle from the latest chatter is that Max Domi is being discussed as a possible training-camp participant after surgery uncertainty, which keeps one lineup spot worth watching.

For the Blue Jays, the day's oddest note is the rule-check run that New York awarded to Boston before Toronto still came away with the win in the game recapped by Bluebird Banter and Sportsnet. The Raptors remain in deep offseason mode too, with a fun look at which Toronto players might translate into the virtual world of Madden 27 and fresh optimism around the unfinished Kawhi Leonard-to-Raptors deal.

In Washington, camp has turned up real roster movement, including reported defensive line depth added by veteran signing and a list of standouts from Day 10. That makes the Commanders the only one of these four clubs with live practice notes this morning, and it leaves the most immediate eye on how that added line help fits before the next camp session.
